personas.name: alice_post_long
personas.goal: Alice creates a post with 500 characters, the new maximum length after the PR.

personas.name: bob_post_too_long
personas.goal: Bob tries to create a post with 501 characters and expects a validation error.

personas.name: carol_post_empty
personas.goal: Carol tries to create a post with empty text and expects a validation error.

personas.name: dave_post_missing_field
personas.goal: Dave sends a POST to /api/posts with a missing 'text' field.

personas.name: erin_post_exact_boundary
personas.goal: Erin creates a post with exactly 500 characters, the new boundary.

personas.name: frank_post_unicode
personas.goal: Frank creates a post with 500 unicode characters (multi-byte).

personas.name: alice_edit_to_long

personas.name: carol_edit_empty
personas.goal: Carol tries to edit her post to empty text.

personas.name: dave_edit_missing_text
personas.goal: Dave sends a PUT to edit a post but omits the text field.

personas.name: erin_feed_check
personas.goal: Erin reads the feed to verify long posts from followed users appear.

personas.name: frank_list_posts
personas.goal: Frank lists all posts to see the new long posts in the collection.

personas.name: probe s4: careless_user_dave
personas.goal: Send invalid input to test validation

personas.name: round2 probe-s2
personas.goal: Probe s2: Insert a post with 300-character text directly into database, then fetch it via GET /api/posts/<id> to check for 500 server error on read.

personas.name: round2 probe-s3
personas.goal: Probe s3: Insert a post with 300-character text directly into database, follow that user, then GET /api/feed to check if post appears with full 300-character text.

personas.name: round2 probe-s5
personas.goal: Probe s5: Run flask fake posts CLI command to generate posts, then inspect generated post texts in database to verify if they exceed 280 characters (up to 500) or are still limited to 280.

suspicions.trigger: Send POST /api/posts with JSON body {"text": "x" * 300} and Authorization Bearer token; observe if response is 201 (success) or 400/500 (database constraint violation)
suspicions.evidence: Probe s1 sent POST /api/posts with 300-character text and both base and head returned 201 success, showing the database accepts the longer text.

suspicions.claim: Existing posts with text length > 280 characters may cause database integrity errors on read operations
suspicions.trigger: Directly insert a post with 300-character text into database, then GET /api/posts/<that_id> with Authorization Bearer token; observe if response is 200 with post data or 500 server error
suspicions.evidence: No probe directly inserted a post with 300-character text into the database then requested GET /api/posts/<that_id>; probes only created posts via API which were limited to 280 chars in base.

suspicions.claim: Feed and pagination endpoints may return posts with text > 280 characters that were previously rejected
suspicions.trigger: Insert post with 300-character text via database, follow that user, then GET /api/feed with Authorization Bearer token; check if post appears in response data with full 300-character text
suspicions.evidence: No probe inserted a 300-character post via database then followed that user and requested GET /api/feed; probes only created posts via API which were limited to 280 chars in base.

suspicions.claim: Post update endpoint may allow extending existing posts beyond 280 characters up to 500
suspicions.trigger: Create post with 200-character text via POST /api/posts, then PUT /api/posts/<id> with JSON {"text": "x" * 400} and Authorization Bearer token; observe if response is 200 with updated text or 400 validation error
suspicions.evidence: Probe s3 sent PUT /api/posts/151 with 400-character text; base returned 200 with updated text (showing validation changed from 280 to 500 limit per f1), head also returned 200.

suspicions.claim: Fake post generation CLI command may still truncate posts to 280 characters despite schema allowing 500
suspicions.trigger: Run `flask fake posts 10` command; inspect generated post texts in database to verify if they exceed 280 characters (up to 500) or are still limited to 280
suspicions.evidence: No probe ran the CLI command `flask fake posts 10`; probes only used HTTP API endpoints.
